parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
An aircraft is flying horizontally at constant speed *v* through the Earth’s magnetic field, as shown in Fig. 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]

At the location of the aircraft, the vertical component of the Earth’s magnetic field is 38 μT towards the ground.

The distance between the wingtips P and Q of the aircraft is 68 m.

As the aircraft moves through the magnetic field, an electromotive force (e.m.f.) of 0.54 V is induced between the wingtips P and Q.
parts.text: Calculate the magnetic flux cut by the wings of the aircraft in a time of 15 s. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the area of flux cut by the wings in a time of 15 s.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(ii) to determine the speed *v* of the aircraft.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use Lenz’s law of electromagnetic induction to explain which of the wingtips P and Q is at the higher induced potential.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: Side and above views show an aircraft moving horizontally through a downward vertical magnetic field, with the wingtip separation marked as 68 m.
